small_guidance:
- The inner loop iterates `KH*KW*ceil(IC/BLOCK_IC)` times per OHW tile with BLOCK_OHW=256; raise BLOCK_OHW to 1024 and BLOCK_IC to 64 to amortize index math and increase arithmetic intensity. Add `triton.autotune` over BLOCK_OHW ∈ {512,1024,2048}, BLOCK_IC ∈ {32,64}, num_warps ∈ {4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3}.
- Hoist `oh*IW`, `ih*IW`, and the per-(kh,kw) `(num_h%STRIDE_H==0)` checks out of the IC loop (they don't depend on ic) — currently they're recomputed per ic_start tile inside the kh/kw loops.
- Preload the weight slice `w[:, oc, kh, kw]` for all (kh,kw) into registers once per program (only KH*KW*IC = 9*64 = 576 fp32 values), eliminating the repeated `tl.load` of weights inside the OHW-tile loop.
large_guidance:
- The current strategy is gather-based (one program per (N, OC), looping the full OH*OW=256*256 output grid times KH*KW*IC). That's the right asymptotic work but parallelism is only N*OC = 16*128 = 2048 programs, each doing ~9*64*65536 ≈ 38M FMAs — far too serial. Rewrite as a scatter-add: one program per (N, IC tile, IH*IW tile) computes input×weight outer products and atomically accumulates a per-(N, OC) partial sum, then a tiny second kernel applies bias and the 1/(OH*OW)*multiplier scale. This exposes N*IC*IH*IW = 16*64*128*128 ≈ 16M-element parallelism instead of 2K.
- Alternatively, since the final output is just (N, OC, 1, 1), fold the spatial mean directly into the accumulation: each program handles a tile of input (n, ic_tile, ih_tile, iw_tile) and an OC tile, computes the contribution `Σ_{kh,kw} w[ic,oc,kh,kw] * x[n,ic,ih,iw] * count(valid_output_positions)` — but every input element contributes to exactly KH*KW output positions (modulo boundary), and the boundary count is cheap to compute. Use atomic-add into a (N, OC) buffer. This keeps the full multiply-accumulate count (asymptotically same as conv-transpose) while collapsing the OH*OW gather.
- Use channels-last (NHWC) input layout so the IC reduction is the contiguous axis; the GEMM-K dimension (IC*KH*KW = 576) then loads coalesced and a tl.dot over [BLOCK_OHW, BLOCK_K] x [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_OC] becomes feasible (current kernel does no tl.dot at all).
